I really like my new doctor at women center. Dr. Taviwan, she only works on Saturday. My first time to check up with her. The hospital system a bit slow but a must booked in advance. No parking space in the building. But on the side road opposite has some parking space. Also details of all the Doctors not quite clear of education, history of work and professional file.
Administration workers need to improve on the website. It’s poor work.
very very good. I got a wound from accident, they cure my wound very quick and very professional. I felt only a bit pain after the surgery, thank you

Been waiting to see the ENT doctor for more than 2 hours and when asked the reception, the only response is to JUST WAIT TILL YOUR TIME Zzzz
There is no accurate effort and absolutely no respect to the patients and the clock.

P.s; We got 2 mins of counselling with a doctor(not even an expertise) after waiting for 7 hours.
And still had to wait for like whole day for the next appointment and to take pills.
Need to wait sooo long (approximately 2 hours just to meet with Dr for few minutes). Really sad about the queue system. Very very long

Overall if you want to see real Thai health care it is not world superior on the government level. It's really poor. Dirty old and long que even with appointment. It is no different than in cities in India or Africa. They overload the staff but Because the government forces good doctors to come in - many Thai people will choose to come. But overall the actual staff on government pay are as low quality as any other sector.
Twice I experienced xenophobia directly - in my family being pushed last in the appointment card. That means I was scheduled at 9am and saw the whole room rotate all day and I was seen at 4pm.
Multiple times my family was the only one skipped over to not receive free masks or candies for kids.
The facility is held by threads and is an embarrassment to the community overall more to Thailand as a country.

-The stretcher bearers at the Sripat Building are attentive and prioritize the well-being of patients. They push the stretcher smoothly over uneven surfaces, are polite, and never make you feel uncomfortable. …

We donated blood for charity.
We're foreigners, and they accepted us without any problems.
You need a passport and be in good health.
There was no line; we were the first ones there at 8 a.m.
We filled out a form. They took a blood sample from my finger and gave me iron supplements.
We donated blood, then were treated to sweet drinks and cookies.
The most annoying thing is, I didn't know I already had dengue; I got sick the next day. I felt fine during the donation.

My experience with medical care here was terrible. They didn't tell me what tests I needed or what the costs were, but instead arranged for a lot of tests on me, many of which were completely unnecessary and very expensive. It was completely unreasonable. In the end, they just sent me a text message with the test results, telling me that everything was fine. That was all they said, without any important information.
The building is a bit old, but having a Chinese translator with me made me feel safe. Recommended for dialysis in Chiang Mai.
The pediatric care here is excellent. The medicine is good, the service is good, it's clean, and the service is outstanding.
Gynecology Clinic, Sripathana Center, 13th floor, very good service, very attentive to patients.

There are specialist doctors.
The place is clean and convenient.
